MotifEngine

The motif engine: builds impossible isometric shapes from lattice bars and cubes with declared crossings, and renders them as flat-filled SVG in any of the six palette families. A function library with no visual output of its own; MotifLoader and MotifPattern build on it. Also exported one function at a time.

Live example

The example needs JavaScript; the usage below shows the markup.

Usage

The motif engine — a function library with no visual output of its own. It builds impossible isometric shapes in the language of the cubo impossível (lattice bars and cubes, shaded top lightest, left mid, right darkest) and returns them as data or as an SVG string, in any of the six palette families. MotifLoader and MotifPattern are built on it; reach for those first. Use the engine directly only to place a generated shape the components do not cover.

Exported functions (also grouped on the MotifEngine object):

  • isoPoint(p) — lattice point [x, y, z] to screen point (z up, x at +30°, y at −30°).
  • motifBar(axis, start, length, thickness?) and motifCube(at, size?) — the two primitives.
  • makeMotifShape(name, parts, crossings?) — a shape; a crossing { over, under, overAt } says part over passes in front of under at its overAt end and behind at the other. Everything else paints by plain geometry (what is behind paints first). A part may be over in one crossing and under in another, so an impossible loop is declared the natural way, one crossing per joint (A over B, B over C, C over A). Crossings beat geometry; the first declared wins a contradiction.
  • motifFaces(shape) — every visible face in paint order.
  • motifPieces(shape, hue) — faces grouped per piece and filled from the palette ramp; null for an unknown hue.
  • motifToSvg(shape, { hue, size?, title? }) — one <svg> string; '' for an unknown hue.
  • motifShapes and motifShapeNames — the generated shape library, ready to pass to motifToSvg (and the default source of shapes for MotifLoader and MotifPattern).
  • renderMotifPattern(opts) — library shapes tiled into one full-bleed <svg> string (the engine behind MotifPattern): shape (a name or a list), width, height, cell (96), gap (0), layout (grid, brick, isometric), fill (0–1), seed (1), hue or hues with sequence (row, diagonal, seeded), opacity (1), animate (none, reveal, ambient). '' for an unknown shape or hue; never throws. At most MAX_PATTERN_CELLS (1500) cells: a smaller cell is enlarged until it fits. width, height and cell are clamped to 1e9. The <svg> declares xmlns:xlink and every <use> carries both href and xlink:href, because older Safari, Inkscape 0.92, old librsvg and some print pipelines resolve only the latter.

Generated shapes — gerados pelo sistema, não fornecidos pelo Sesc; the six official constructions stay in BrandMotif:

NameDescrição
cubeO cubo da gramática, em moldura de doze barras.
triangleTriângulo de Penrose: três barras que se fecham sem poder.
stairEscada sem fim: sobe dois lances e volta ao começo.
loopLaço de cinco barras que sobe e nunca desce.
towerTorre de Escher: a coluna de trás passa pela frente.
twinDois cubos gêmeos encaixados de um jeito impossível.
import { motifShapes, motifToSvg } from '@idcesares/rse-design-system';
const svg = motifToSvg(motifShapes.triangle, { hue: 'purple', size: 96 });
import { motifBar, motifCube, makeMotifShape, motifToSvg } from '@idcesares/rse-design-system';

const shape = makeMotifShape('bridge', [
  motifBar('x', [0, 0, 0], 4),
  motifBar('y', [2, -2, 1], 4),  // rests on the first bar, so geometry puts it in front…
  motifCube([0, 2, 0]),
], [{ over: 0, under: 1, overAt: 'end' }]);  // …and the crossing brings the first bar's end over it

// Decorative (aria-hidden):
const svg = motifToSvg(shape, { hue: 'orange', size: 160 });
// Carrying meaning: the title is read out, in pt-BR.
const named = motifToSvg(shape, { hue: 'blue', size: 160, title: 'Forma impossível da Rede' });

A pattern field — decorative, so it is aria-hidden; text goes on a solid panel beside or over it, never on the cells:

import { renderMotifPattern } from '@idcesares/rse-design-system';

// Faixa de fundo do hero "Matrículas abertas": cubos no reticulado isométrico, três cores em diagonal.
const fundo = renderMotifPattern({
  shape: 'cube', width: 1440, height: 480, cell: 96, gap: 8,
  layout: 'isometric', hues: ['blue', 'green', 'yellow'], sequence: 'diagonal',
  fill: 0.7, seed: 12, opacity: 0.3,
});

Same options, same SVG (seeded, coordinates rounded to 2 decimals). The SVG fills its box like background-size: cover (preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice") and draws one ring of cells past every edge, so shapes run off the edges instead of stopping short. Each shape's geometry is emitted once in <defs> (id="rse-motif-pattern-<shape>-<hue>", the same drawing wherever that id appears) and every cell is <g class="rse-motif-pattern__cell" style="--d:N"> around a <use>; --d is the cell's stagger step (its distance from the top-left, in cells) and animate only adds data-animate on the <svg>: the motion itself is MotifPattern's CSS. grid and brick fit each shape's box to cell − gap; isometric fits it to the hexagon of its tile, so a cube field locks together like tumbling blocks and other shapes never cover a neighbour.

Duas malhas na mesma página compartilham os mesmos ids (rse-motif-pattern-<forma>-<matiz>) de propósito: o mesmo id é sempre o mesmo desenho. Por isso esses ids não devem ser reutilizados para outro conteúdo na página.

In a static page, the same functions are on window.RSE:

<div id="motif"></div>
<script>
  const { motifCube, makeMotifShape, motifToSvg } = window.RSE;
  document.getElementById('motif').innerHTML =
    motifToSvg(makeMotifShape('cube', [motifCube([0, 0, 0], 2)]), { hue: 'green', size: 96 });
</script>

Rules: colours come only from the palette ramp (light, base, dark); never add gradients, strokes or effects to the output. Generated shapes are system work, not artwork supplied by Sesc: the six official constructions stay in BrandMotif. Same input, same SVG, coordinates rounded to 2 decimals. Every piece is a <g class="rse-motif__piece"> carrying --i (part index) and --ax/--ay (its axis on screen) for motion built on top.
